questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: WANE
questions.x: 'Wane' means diminish. 'Grow' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: The inspector's report was ____ that no further action was needed.
questions.x: Correct answer: so conclusive. 'So + adjective + that' expresses result.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
One of the main reason / for the delay / was the shortage of staff.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'One of the main reason'. 'One of' is followed by a plural noun: 'one of the main reasons'.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To fly off the handle' mean?
questions.x: 'To fly off the handle' means: to lose one's temper suddenly.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Detrimental'.
questions.x: 'Detrimental' is the opposite of 'Beneficial'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Detrimental'.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A government ruled by religious leaders'
questions.x: 'Theocracy' means a government ruled by religious leaders.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Mundane'.
questions.x: 'Mundane' is the opposite of 'Extraordinary'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Mundane'.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Vehement'.
questions.x: 'Vehement' means forceful. 'Mild' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'Too many cooks spoil the broth'
o: Too many people managing a task can ruin it
Food tastes better with more spices
questions.x: 'Too many cooks spoil the broth' means: too many people managing a task can ruin it.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Hardly had the meeting begun / than the fire alarm / went off.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'than the fire alarm'. 'Hardly' is followed by 'when', not 'than'.

questions.q: Why are many elderly people living alone, according to the passage?
questions.x: Answer: 'Young people migrate for work'. Migration of the young is cited. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Old age in India is increasingly lived alone. As young people migrate for work, many elderly parents remain in villages or small towns, managing illness and loneliness without daily help. Pensions provide a measure of independence, but they are not enough. Community centres, home visits by health workers and neighbourhood networks can fill gaps that money alone cannot.

questions.q: What is the author's view about pensions?
o: They solve all problems of old age
They provide independence but must be complemented by community support
questions.x: Answer: 'They provide independence but must be complemented by community support'. The passage says pensions are 'not enough' and lists other supports. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Old age in India is increasingly lived alone. As young people migrate for work, many elderly parents remain in villages or small towns, managing illness and loneliness without daily help. Pensions provide a measure of independence, but they are not enough. Community centres, home visits by health workers and neighbourhood networks can fill gaps that money alone cannot.

questions.q: Madan Lal Dhingra assassinated which official in London in 1909?
questions.x: Correct answer: Curzon Wyllie. Dhingra was associated with India House.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons?
questions.x: Correct answer: Dadabhai Naoroji. He was elected from Finsbury Central as a Liberal in 1892.

questions.q: Who led the 1930 Salt Satyagraha in Kerala at Payyannur?
questions.x: Correct answer: K. Kelappan. Kelappan is known as 'Kerala Gandhi'.

questions.q: The Wahabi movement in India was associated with:
questions.x: Correct answer: Syed Ahmad of Rae Bareli. Patna was its centre.

questions.q: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in:
questions.x: It received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

questions.q: Who presided over the 1905 session of the Indian National Congress held at Benares?
questions.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the 1905 Benares session — the session that supported the Swadeshi and boycott in Bengal.

questions.q: Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in 1940 in London to avenge:
questions.x: Correct answer: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre. O'Dwyer was Lieutenant Governor of Punjab in 1919.

questions.q: Madam Bhikaji Cama unfurled an Indian flag at the International Socialist Congress held in 1907 at:
questions.x: It was one of the earliest flags of Indian independence raised abroad.

questions.q: The Swaraj Party was formed to:
o: Enter the legislatures and obstruct them from within
Support the British in World War I
questions.x: Correct answer: Enter the legislatures and obstruct them from within. C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru were the 'pro-changers'.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: the Communal Award was announced by Ramsay MacDonald.
questions.x: The Communal Award was announced by Ramsay MacDonald in 1932. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: The 'Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain' campaign focuses on:
questions.x: Correct answer: Rainwater harvesting and water conservation. Its tagline is 'Catch the rain, where it falls, when it falls'.

questions.q: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson and James Robinson for studies on:
o: How institutions are formed and affect prosperity
questions.x: Correct answer: How institutions are formed and affect prosperity. Their work explains differences in prosperity between nations.

questions.q: 'Circular migration' refers to:
o: Repeated temporary movement between origin and destination areas
questions.x: Correct answer: Repeated temporary movement between origin and destination areas. Seasonal construction and agricultural workers are examples.

questions.q: The 'U-WIN' portal is meant for:
o: Digitally registering and tracking routine immunisation
questions.x: Correct answer: Digitally registering and tracking routine immunisation. It is modelled on the CoWIN platform.

questions.q: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was shared by David Baker, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for work on:
o: Computational protein design and protein structure prediction
questions.x: Correct answer: Computational protein design and protein structure prediction. AlphaFold predicted structures of nearly all known proteins.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 25 December?
questions.x: 25 December is Good Governance Day (Atal Bihari Vajpayee).

questions.q: The new Pamban Bridge, opened in April 2025, is notable as India's first:
questions.x: Correct answer: Vertical-lift railway sea bridge. It connects Rameswaram (Pamban Island) to the mainland.

questions.q: India's longest sea bridge, Atal Setu (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link), was opened in:
questions.x: Correct answer: January 2024. It connects Sewri in Mumbai with Nhava Sheva.

questions.q: The headquarters of the BIMSTEC Secretariat is located in:
questions.x: BIMSTEC Secretariat: headquartered in Dhaka.

questions.q: The 'Henley Passport Index' is published by:
questions.x: 'Henley Passport Index' is brought out by Henley & Partners.

questions.q: Article 315 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States
Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession
questions.x: Article 315: Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States.

questions.q: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution contains:
o: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (29 subjects)
questions.x: Eleventh Schedule: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (29 subjects).

questions.q: Which High Court has jurisdiction over the largest number of States/UTs?
questions.x: Correct answer: Guwahati High Court. It covers Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
questions.x: In Berubari (1960) it had said the Preamble was not part of the Constitution; Kesavananda reversed that view.

questions.q: Article 63 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights
Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution
Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
questions.x: Article 63: The Vice-President of India.

questions.q: The Right to Information Act was enacted in:
questions.x: The RTI Act is rooted in Article 19(1)(a); the Central Information Commission hears appeals.

questions.q: Which of the following can be introduced in either House of Parliament?
o: A Finance Bill containing only Article 110 matters
questions.x: Correct answer: A Constitution Amendment Bill. Amendment bills may originate in either House (Article 368).

questions.q: Reservation of seats for women in Panchayats under the 73rd Amendment is not less than:
questions.x: Correct answer: One-third. Many States have raised it to 50%.

questions.q: The President's power to grant pardon extends to:
o: All cases where the sentence is by a court martial and death sentences
questions.x: Article 72; the Governor under Article 161 cannot pardon death sentences or court-martial sentences.

questions.q: The Solicitor General of India is a:
o: Post created by the Supreme Court
questions.x: Correct answer: Statutory post (not a constitutional office). Only the Attorney-General is mentioned in the Constitution.

questions.q: A fixed deposit pays 12% per annum while inflation is 6%. Using the Fisher approximation, the real rate of interest is about:
questions.x:
Fisher approximation: real rate ≈ nominal rate − inflation = 12 − 6 = 6%.
(Exact: (1.12/1.06 − 1) × 100 ≈ 5.66%.)

questions.q: 'Revenue deficit' arises when:
questions.x: Correct answer: Revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipts. It indicates borrowing to finance consumption.

questions.q: Which agency releases GDP estimates in India?
questions.x: Correct answer: National Statistics Office (MoSPI). The NSO releases advance, provisional and revised estimates.

questions.q: The 'Atal Innovation Mission' is set up under:
questions.x: Correct answer: NITI Aayog. It runs Atal Tinkering Labs in schools.

questions.q: Demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes was announced on:
questions.x: The RBI later withdrew ₹2,000 notes from circulation in May 2023 (they remain legal tender).

questions.q: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) insures bank deposits up to:
questions.x: Correct answer: ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank. The limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh in 2020.

questions.q: NITI Aayog's 'SDG India Index' ranks:
o: States and Union Territories on progress towards the SDGs
questions.x: Correct answer: States and Union Territories on progress towards the SDGs. Kerala and Uttarakhand have topped recent editions.

questions.q: Payment banks in India can:
o: Accept deposits up to a limit and issue debit cards, but cannot lend
questions.x: Correct answer: Accept deposits up to a limit and issue debit cards, but cannot lend. The deposit limit is ₹2 lakh per customer.

questions.q: The RBI was nationalised — in which year?
questions.x: The RBI was nationalised in 1949.

questions.q: Startup India was launched in:
questions.x: Correct answer: January 2016. 16 January is now observed as National Startup Day.

questions.q: Which of the following causes the pass book balance to be higher than the cash book balance?
o: Bank charges debited by the bank
Cheques issued but not yet presented for payment
A dishonoured cheque not recorded in the cash book
Cheques deposited but not yet collected
questions.x: The cash book has already reduced the balance, but the bank has not yet paid.

questions.q: Heavy advertising expenditure on launching a new product, whose benefit lasts several years, may be treated as:
o: Capital expenditure on a tangible asset
Deferred revenue expenditure (written off over years, as permitted)
questions.x: Large non-recurring revenue expenditure with long-lasting benefits was traditionally deferred; current standards generally expense such costs.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹10,000, Debtors ₹80,000, Inventory ₹95,000, Prepaid expenses ₹10,000, Creditors ₹50,000, Bills payable ₹5,000 and Outstanding expenses ₹5,000. Its current ratio is:
P and Q share profits in the ratio 5 : 4. They admit R for a 1/6 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
Costs that remain constant in total irrespective of output (within a range) are:
questions.x: Correct answer: Fixed costs. Fixed cost per unit falls as output rises.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹5,500 at the beginning of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 6% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 5,500 = ₹66,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the beginning of each month = 6.5 months.
Interest = 66,000 × 6% × 6.5/12 = ₹2,145.

questions.q: Provision for doubtful debts is created on the basis of:
o: Conservatism, to provide for anticipated losses
questions.x: Correct answer: Conservatism, to provide for anticipated losses. It is shown as a deduction from debtors and charged to P&L.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹76,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹5,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹1,000. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹76,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 5,000
− Cheques deposited not credited 1,000
Pass book balance = ₹80,000.

questions.q: A computer server is purchased for ₹2,05,000 and ₹5,000 is spent on its installation. Its estimated useful life is 8 years with a residual value of ₹14,000. Annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method is:
questions.x:
SLM depreciation = (Cost + installation − residual value) / useful life.
= (2,05,000 + 5,000 − 14,000) / 8 = 1,96,000 / 8 = ₹24,500 per year.
Installation is capitalised as part of cost (AS 10 / Ind AS 16).

questions.q: Under Section 53 of the Companies Act, 2013, a company generally cannot issue shares at a:
questions.x: Correct answer: Discount (except sweat equity shares). Issue at a discount is void except for sweat equity shares.

questions.q: Interest accrued but not received on investments is recorded as:
o: Interest A/c Dr. To Accrued Interest A/c
Accrued Interest A/c Dr. To Interest A/c
Cash A/c Dr. To Interest A/c
Investment A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
questions.x: Correct answer: Accrued Interest A/c Dr. To Interest A/c. Accrued income is an asset; income is credited.

questions.q: In the absence of an agreement, interest on a partner's loan to the firm is allowed at:
questions.x: Section 13(d) of the Partnership Act provides 6% p.a. on advances beyond capital.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 150 units @ ₹20; 10th — 300 units @ ₹23; 20th — 200 units @ ₹27. 200 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 450 units left come from the latest purchases: 200 × ₹27 + 250 × ₹23 = ₹11,150.

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹75,000, closing inventory is ₹45,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹3,60,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (75,000 + 45,000) / 2 = ₹60,000.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 3,60,000 / 60,000 = 6 times.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'welfare facility' required under the OSH Code (subject to thresholds)?
questions.x: Welfare facilities include canteens, creches, first-aid, washing, sitting arrangements, shelters and lunch rooms, subject to prescribed thresholds.

questions.q: Short-term unemployment while workers move between jobs is known as:
questions.x: Frictional unemployment is temporary and exists even at full employment.

questions.q: The Labour Bureau, which compiles CPI-IW, functions under the Ministry of:
questions.x: The Labour Bureau, with offices at Shimla and Chandigarh, is an attached office of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (formerly the Employment Linked Incentive scheme) covers jobs created during:
questions.x: The Cabinet approved the scheme in July 2025 with an outlay of about ₹99,446 crore; it is operated through EPFO.

questions.q: Which schedule of the Employees' Compensation Act lists occupational diseases?
questions.x: Schedule III lists occupational diseases (Parts A, B, C); Schedule I lists injuries with percentage loss of earning capacity, Schedule II lists persons included as employees.

questions.q: Which 1993 Supreme Court case held that the principles of natural justice must be followed even when standing orders provide for automatic termination for overstaying leave?
o: Uptron India Ltd v. Shammi Bhan (1998)
D.K. Yadav v. J.M.A. Industries Ltd
questions.x: D.K. Yadav applied Article 21 and natural justice to termination of services.

questions.q: The ILO's 'Decent Work Agenda' (1999) rests on four strategic pillars. Which is NOT one of them?
questions.x: The four pillars are employment creation, rights at work, social protection and social dialogue.

questions.q: For a fortnightly wage period, the Code on Wages requires payment:
o: Within 48 hours of a written demand
On the 15th and last day of the month regardless of the wage period
Within seven days of the fortnight
Before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight
questions.x: Fortnightly wages must be paid before the end of the second day after the fortnight closes.

questions.q: The Code on Wages requires minimum wage rates to be reviewed or revised by the appropriate government ordinarily at an interval not exceeding:
questions.x: Section 8(4): minimum rates are to be reviewed/revised ordinarily at intervals not exceeding five years.

questions.q: In Herzberg's two-factor theory, which of the following is a 'hygiene factor'?
questions.x: Hygiene factors (pay, policy, supervision, conditions) prevent dissatisfaction; motivators (achievement, recognition, work itself, responsibility, advancement) create satisfaction.

questions.q: The 'Factories Act, 1948' defined an adult as a person who has completed:
questions.x: Under the Factories Act, an adult had completed 18 years; an adolescent was 15–18 and a child below 15 (now harmonised with the child labour law).

questions.q: Under the child labour law as amended in 2016, an 'adolescent' means a person who has completed 14 years of age but not completed:
questions.x: Adolescents are 14–18 years; they may not be employed in hazardous occupations and processes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about platform workers under the Code on Social Security:
1. Platform work is a subset of gig work accessed through online platforms.
2. Aggregators are required to share details of platform workers for registration.
3. Platform workers automatically become employees of the aggregator.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Code does not deem platform workers to be employees; it creates a separate social security framework funded partly by aggregators.

questions.q: ILO Convention No. 189 (2011) relates to:
questions.x: C189 sets standards for decent work for domestic workers.

questions.q: A 'sympathetic strike' is one in which:
o: Workers strike for one hour only
Workers strike in support of workers of another establishment without their own grievance
questions.x: Sympathetic strikes express solidarity; their legality depends on statutory notice rules.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about standing orders under the IR Code:
1. The Central Government prepares model standing orders.
2. If an establishment adopts the model standing orders, they are deemed certified.
3. Standing orders apply to establishments with 50 or more workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Model standing orders are framed by the Centre; adopted model orders are deemed certified. Applicability is 300 or more workers, not 50.

questions.q:
Consider the following thresholds under the Code on Social Security:
1. EPF — 20 employees
2. ESI — 10 employees
3. Gratuity — 10 employees
4. Creche (maternity benefit) — 50 employees
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.x:
4 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
All four thresholds are correct.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) provides cash incentive of ₹5,000 to pregnant and lactating women for:
o: The first living child (and ₹6,000 for a second child if it is a girl, under PMMVY 2.0)
questions.x: PMMVY (2017) compensates wage loss; PMMVY 2.0 under Mission Shakti extends benefit to a second girl child.

questions.q: Of the employer's 12% EPF contribution for a member earning up to the wage ceiling, how much goes to the pension fund (EPS)?
questions.x: 8.33% goes to EPS (capped at ₹1,250 a month); the remaining 3.67% stays in the EPF account.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹720. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 26-week period including Sundays: 26 × 7 = 182 days.
Amount = ₹720 × 182 = ₹1,31,040. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹1,12,320.)

questions.q: The unique account number allotted to an NPS subscriber is the:
questions.x: Correct answer: PRAN (Permanent Retirement Account Number). Each NPS subscriber gets a 12-digit PRAN.

questions.q: EPFO's 'e-Nomination' facility allows members to:
o: Nominate family members online with Aadhaar-based e-sign
Change their date of birth without proof
questions.x: Online nomination helps quick settlement of PF, EPS and EDLI on the member's death.

questions.q: An employee retires after 28 years and 10 months of continuous service. Last drawn monthly wages (basic + DA) are ₹44,000. Gratuity payable under the statutory formula (non-seasonal establishment) is:
questions.x:
Gratuity = 15/26 × last drawn wages × completed years of service.
10 months is more than six months, so it counts as a full year → 29 years.
= 15/26 × 44,000 × 29 = ₹7,36,154 (well within the ₹20 lakh ceiling).
The divisor 26 reflects working days in a month.

questions.q: Which of the following schemes is 'non-contributory' for the beneficiary?
questions.x: PM-JAY is fully government-funded; APY, PMJJBY and EPF require contributions/premiums.

questions.q: The Central Government's contribution to the Employees' Pension Scheme is:
questions.x: The Centre contributes 1.16% of the member's wages (up to the ceiling) to the Pension Fund.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): ESIC provides medical benefit to the family members of insured persons.
Reason (R): ESI is a comprehensive social insurance scheme covering health and cash benefits.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains why family members are covered — ESI is a comprehensive scheme.

questions.q: The two contribution periods under the ESI scheme are:
o: January to June and July to December
1 April to 30 September and 1 October to 31 March
questions.x: Corresponding benefit periods are 1 January–30 June and 1 July–31 December.

questions.q: 'Longevity risk' in pensions refers to the risk that:
o: Pension funds fail due to fraud
People outlive their savings because they live longer than expected
questions.x: Annuities and DB pensions protect against longevity risk; lump-sum DC withdrawals do not.

questions.q: The bending of light when it passes from one medium to another is called:
questions.x: A straw appears bent in a glass of water due to refraction.

questions.q: 'Charles Babbage' is known as the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Father of the computer. He designed the Analytical Engine.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Wide Area Network'?
questions.x: Wide Area Network is abbreviated as WAN.

questions.q: The default file extension of a Microsoft Word document (2007 onwards) is:
questions.x: Correct answer: .docx. .xlsx is Excel and .pptx PowerPoint.

questions.q: The layer of the atmosphere closest to the Earth, where weather occurs, is the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Troposphere. The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere.

questions.q: CaOCl₂ (calcium oxychloride) is commonly known as:
questions.x: CaOCl₂ (calcium oxychloride) is bleaching powder.

questions.q: A person standing in a lift that accelerates upward feels:
questions.x: Correct answer: Heavier than usual. Apparent weight = m(g + a) when accelerating upward.

questions.q: The decimal value of binary 101010 is:
A 'Trojan horse' is malware that:
questions.x: Correct answer: Disguises itself as legitimate software. A worm self-replicates across networks.

questions.q: Which mineral is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.x: Iron deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: Bose–Einstein statistics is credited to:
questions.x: Bose–Einstein statistics: Satyendra Nath Bose.

questions.q: IPv4 addresses are how many bits long?
questions.x: Correct answer: 32 bits. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses.

questions.q: A invests ₹45,000 for the whole year and B invests ₹60,000 after 6 months. If the annual profit is ₹2,500, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 45,000×12, B: 60,000×6 → 3 : 2.
B's share = 2/5 × 2,500 = ₹1,000.

questions.q: 2 June 2020 was a Tuesday. What day of the week was 2 June 2024?
questions.x:
Each ordinary year shifts the day by 1, and a leap day (29 Feb) crossed in between adds 1 more.
Total days between the dates = 1461 = 208 weeks + 5 odd days.
Tuesday + 5 = Sunday.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 60% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. His gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Let CP = 100. Marked price = 160.
SP after 10% discount = 160 × 0.9 = 144.
Gain = 144 − 100 = 44 on 100 → 44% gain.
Shortcut: m − d − md/100 = 60 − 10 − 6 = 44%.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 7 : 5. After 14 years, the ratio will become 7 : 6. What is P's present age?
In how many ways can the letters of the word 'WELFARE' be arranged so that all the vowels always come together?
questions.x:
Vowels: E, A, E; consonants: W, L, F, R.
Treat the vowels as one block → 5 units → 120 arrangements (all letters are distinct).
Vowels inside the block: 3 ways (E appears 2 times).
Total = 120 × 3 = 360.

questions.q: If A : B = 3 : 6 and B : C = 2 : 4, and a sum of ₹1,050 is shared among A, B and C in that combined ratio, C receives:
What is the least number which, when divided by 9, 15, 8, leaves a remainder of 4 in each case?
questions.x: Required number = LCM(9, 15, 8) + 4 = 360 + 4 = 364.

questions.q: The average weight of 17 parcels is 46 kg. When one more parcel is added, the average becomes 48 kg. The weight of the new parcel is:
questions.x:
Old total = 17 × 46 = 782 kg. New total = 18 × 48 = 864 kg.
New parcel = 864 − 782 = 82 kg.
Shortcut: new value = new average + (increase × old count) = 48 + 2 × 17 = 82 kg.

questions.q: Find the median of the daily claims received: 28, 32, 31, 89, 20, 42, 30, 94, 60, 68.
questions.x:
Arrange in order: 20, 28, 30, 31, 32, 42, 60, 68, 89, 94.
n = 10 (even) → median = average of the 5th and 6th values = (32 + 42)/2 = 37.

questions.q: There are 66 names in a merit list. Nisha's name is 30th from the top. What is its position from the bottom?
questions.x: Position from bottom = Total − position from top + 1 = 66 − 30 + 1 = 37.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 9, 10, 14, 23, 39, ?
questions.x: Differences are 1², 2², 3², 4² (1, 4, 9, 16). Next difference = 5² = 25 → 39 + 25 = 64.

questions.q: Ravi can file the returns of a branch in 27 days and Kiran in 54 days. They start together, but Ravi leaves after 2 days. In how many days in all is the work completed?
questions.x:
Work done together in 2 days = 2 × (1/27 + 1/54) = 2/18 = 1/9.
Remaining = 8/9, done by Kiran alone in 8/9 × 54 = 48 days.
Total = 2 + 48 = 50 days.

questions.q: A field officer starts from point O and walks 8 km towards South, then turns left and walks 1 km, then turns right and walks 7 km, and finally turns left and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -8 -7 = -15 km → 15 km South.
East–West: +1 +7 = 8 km → 8 km East.
Distance = √(8² + 15²) = 17 km, towards South-East.

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2020: 240  |  2021: 250  |  2022: 270  |  2023: 320  |  2024: 300.
What is the percentage change from 2021 to 2024?
questions.x:
Change = 300 − 250 = 50 on a base of 250 (earlier year).
% change = 50/250 × 100 = 20% → 20% increase.
